The profile is a MODEL, not a measurement: a Gaussian Br(z) and the classical closure Ez ∝ Br2, which follows from electron mobility across the field going as 1/B2 at fixed discharge current. Real cross-field transport is anomalous and faster, so the shape here is qualitatively right and quantitatively soft. The peak field is drawn at 150 G, the right order for a thruster this size. In hardware the peak is put where it is by the pole geometry, and moved from there by the balance between the inner and outer coils.

Efficiency

Three things go wrong between the propellant line and the beam, and the thruster's efficiency is their product. Gas that leaves without ever being ionized; electrons that cross the field to the anode and are paid for without pushing anything; and ions born partway down the fall, which never see all of it.

Three factors, not all of them. Beam divergence and multiply-charged ions cost a real thruster several points more, which is why the product here sits above the 50% or so an SPT actually reaches. The neutral flux is eaten at a rate set by one number, the e-foldings above; the electron leak to the anode is taken as going like 1/B2, calibrated to about 77% at 150 G. Both are SCALINGS, not transport calculations, and the second one in particular is the quantity real Hall thrusters are anomalous in. Nothing here charges for putting the fall outside the channel either, so pushing the peak downstream looks free on this ledger and is not.

Components
Magnetic coreSoft-iron back plate, center stem, pole walls and four outer poles; the outer wall is the skin
Magnetic coilsOne copper ring on the center stem, four discrete solenoids on the outer poles
Discharge channelBoron nitride ceramic cup, closed at the upstream end
AnodeBaseplate injector: 8 orifices, two opposed feeds
Propellant feedAluminum lines, two opposed inlets to the anode plenum
Neutralizer cathodeRefractory tube and tungsten insert; only the snout stands proud of the housing
Cathode housingStainless keeper enclosure, cylindrical over the cathode, on a slab carried clear of the thruster

Illustrative geometry, modeled from an axisymmetric SPT section schematic. Not any real thruster's dimensions.
